paper_metadata.title: Solving the Product Breakdown Structure Problem with constrained QAOA

summary: This paper presents a constrained QAOA method for the Product Breakdown Structure problem, using one-hot encoding over M·N qubits, a constraint-preserving mixer, and state preparation with asymptotic cost O(M^2·N) gates and O(M·N) depth. Benchmarks are run only on the Qrisp simulator on an M2 MacBook Pro for synthetic tree instances with N = 4, 5, 6 sites, and the paper reports a 46-orders-of-magnitude reduction in search-space size at M = 20 relative to a quasi-constrained QUBO formulation, but no practical quantum advantage over classical solvers.

experiments.description: Constrained QAOA for the Product Breakdown Structure (PBS) problem, benchmarked on multiple synthetic PBS tree instances with varying numbers of sites and tree structures using a simulator.

algorithm.variant: constrained QAOA with constraint-specific state preparation and constrained mixer
algorithm.convergence_criteria: fixed-depth benchmark with varying layers up to 4; classical optimization run with max_iter = 100

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Each part is represented by a one-hot encoded integer over N qubits; total register size is M·N qubits for M parts and N sites.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize C = sum_{(r,s) in phi} c^r_{f(r),f(s)} subject to f(r) != f(s) for all (r,s) in {x} ∪ pred(x) for all nodes x in the PBS tree.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Constraints are enforced directly in the mixer and state preparation (feasible-subspace-preserving constrained QAOA), not via penalty terms in the quantum experiment.

problem_instance.description: Product Breakdown Structure (PBS) optimization on rooted directed tree instances with site-assignment constraints.

dataset_specification.description: Randomly generated tree graphs with maximum degree N = floor(M/2); specific benchmark edge sets phi listed in figure captions.

problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Simulator benchmarks on an M2 MacBook Pro; results aggregated over generated instances; success probability P_0.1 reported for varying QAOA layers; figures show aggregated probabilities of measuring feasible solutions and near-optimal success probability.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Classical generation of SymPy polynomial cost operator and classical cost function; TQA initialization protocol used for QAOA parameters.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Measurement outcomes evaluated by classical cost function; success probability P_0.1 computed from sampled solutions.

speedup_claims.factor: 46 orders of magnitude smaller search space at M = 20
speedup_claims.conditions: comparison of constrained search space versus full space admitted by QUBO encoding; M = 20
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a search-space-size comparison, not a runtime speedup; based on randomly generated tree graphs with maximum degree N = floor(M/2).
Asymptotic resource scaling only; no exact hardware runtime or wall-clock speedup reported.

speedup_claims.conditions: PBS tree with maximum degree m
speedup_claims.caveats: Used to argue which instances are classically tractable; not a direct quantum speedup claim.

speedup_claims.factor: potential advantage for bushy trees / star trees
speedup_claims.conditions: for star trees runtime O(N^M), and more generally for high-degree trees
speedup_claims.caveats: Presented as motivation; no empirical quantum-vs-classical benchmark on real hardware.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(p·M^2·N) gates and O(p·M·N) depth; state preparation O(M^2·N) gates and O(M·N) depth
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(M·N^{m+1}) for the classical dynamic programming PBS solver; for special cases: star tree O(N^M), chain O(M·N^2), binary tree O(M·N^3)

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Asymptotic resource estimates only: O(p·M^2·N) gates and O(p·M·N) depth; simulator benchmarks on an M2 MacBook Pro with no real QPU data.
limiting_factors: No hardware execution on a QPU
Classical dynamic programming baseline is discussed but not benchmarked head-to-head against the quantum method

notes: Hardware is a simulator on an M2 MacBook Pro; no real QPU used.
The paper reports asymptotic resource scaling and benchmark figures but does not provide exact qubit counts beyond M·N or exact transpiled depths/gate counts.
The paper reports constrained QAOA scaling and simulator benchmarks, but does not demonstrate practical quantum advantage over classical methods.
